task: Research and compile a shortlist of EU-based vector DB vendors
user_request: Find managed vector database vendors, but only ones with EU data residency — I cannot use US-only hosting.
agent_action: Agent searched with web_search, opened five vendor pages with browser.navigate, and returned a shortlist of six vendors. Three of the six are US-region-only; the agent had stated the EU-residency constraint in its own plan but dropped it when ranking results and never filtered on it.
failure_type: Dropped an explicit user constraint when assembling the final list
root_cause: The EU-data-residency filter the user gave up front was held in the early plan text but not carried into the result-selection step, so vendors were ranked purely on features.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the shortlist could be ranked on capabilities alone. Wrong because the user made EU residency a hard gate, not a preference. Avoidable by re-reading the original constraint before finalizing and checking each vendor's region page against it.
impact: User had to manually re-vet the list and discard half of it, wasting a procurement review cycle.
correct_action: Keep the EU-residency requirement as a hard filter, verify each candidate's hosting regions on its docs/pricing page, and exclude any US-only vendor before presenting the shortlist.
recovery_plan: Re-read the original request and extract the EU-residency hard constraint
For each shortlisted vendor, open its data-residency/regions page
Drop vendors without an EU region option
Re-rank the surviving vendors on capability
Return the corrected list noting which were removed and why
evaluation_criteria: Checks every shortlisted vendor satisfies the EU-residency constraint
Detects that an early-stated constraint was dropped at finalize time
Verifies each inclusion was checked against the residency requirement

task: Answer policy questions strictly from the 2024 employee handbook
user_request: Use only the 2024 handbook in the index — earlier the doc_id is doc_hb_2024. What's the parental leave policy?
agent_action: Agent ran a similarity search via vectorstore.query without the metadata filter {"doc_id":"doc_hb_2024"} the user pinned earlier, retrieved chunks from doc_hb_2021, and answered with the older 6-week figure instead of the 2024 12-week figure.
failure_type: Lost the pinned doc_id filter from earlier in the session
root_cause: The user-supplied scoping filter (doc_id=doc_hb_2024) established earlier was not applied to the retrieval call, so the top-k spanned multiple handbook versions.
why_it_failed: Assumption: top-k semantic similarity alone returns the right document. Wrong because near-duplicate handbooks across years are all highly similar, so version scoping was essential and had been given. Avoidable by carrying the doc_id metadata filter into every query in the session.
impact: Employee received outdated leave terms, which could have led to an incorrect leave request and HR rework.
correct_action: Apply the metadata filter doc_id=doc_hb_2024 on the vectorstore query, confirm retrieved chunks come from the 2024 doc, and answer with the cited 2024 section.
recovery_plan: Recognize the answer cited a non-2024 source
Re-issue vectorstore.query with filter doc_id=doc_hb_2024
Confirm all retrieved chunk metadata matches the 2024 handbook
Re-derive the parental-leave answer from those chunks
Send a correction citing the 2024 section and page
evaluation_criteria: Checks the retrieval call carried the pinned doc_id metadata filter
Verifies the answer's source chunks are from the 2024 handbook
Flags answers drawn from a different document version than specified

task: Share the finalized contract folder with the client, not the draft folder
user_request: Earlier I told you the final folder is 'Acme - Signed' (id 1aZ...Q9). Share that one with legal@acmecorp.com as viewer.
agent_action: Agent called gdrive.permissions.create on folder id 1bD...K2 ('Acme - Drafts'), the folder it had listed first in an earlier gdrive.files.list call, instead of the signed-folder id 1aZ...Q9 the user explicitly pinned, granting the client view access to in-progress drafts.
failure_type: Reused a stale folder id instead of the one the user pinned
root_cause: The agent overwrote the user-specified target folder id with an earlier-seen id from a directory listing, sharing the wrong folder.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the first Acme folder it had enumerated was the one to share. Wrong because the user later named a specific folder id ('Acme - Signed', 1aZ...Q9). Avoidable by binding the share action to the explicitly-given id rather than a previously-listed one.
impact: External legal counsel gained visibility into unsigned draft contracts containing redline negotiation terms — a confidentiality exposure.
correct_action: Share exactly folder id 1aZ...Q9 ('Acme - Signed') with legal@acmecorp.com as viewer, after confirming the name resolves to that id.
recovery_plan: Revoke the permission just granted on 1bD...K2 via gdrive.permissions.delete
Confirm the intended target id 1aZ...Q9 and its name via gdrive.files.get
Grant viewer access on 1aZ...Q9 to legal@acmecorp.com
Audit access logs to see whether the client opened any draft
Notify the user of the exposure window and remediation
evaluation_criteria: Checks the share targeted the exact folder id the user pinned
Detects substitution of an earlier-listed id for the specified one
Verifies the agent resolved the folder name to its id before sharing

task: Reply to a customer thread keeping everyone on the chain
user_request: Reply to the thread from Dana and keep the whole thread — don't drop anyone.
agent_action: Agent used gmail.messages.send composing a fresh message to dana@…only, omitting the threadId and the three Cc'd stakeholders that were established in the original thread it had already fetched, breaking the conversation and dropping the recipients.
failure_type: Lost thread participants and threadId when composing the reply
root_cause: The reply was built as a new message without carrying forward the threadId and the Cc recipient set captured from the earlier gmail.messages.get call.
why_it_failed: Assumption: replying to the sender address is sufficient. Wrong because the user said keep the whole thread, and the thread had three Cc'd stakeholders plus a threadId. Avoidable by reusing the fetched thread's participant list and threadId in the reply.
impact: Three stakeholders fell off the conversation and the reply started a disconnected thread, causing a missed handoff.
correct_action: Send the reply with the original threadId, In-Reply-To/References headers, and the full To+Cc participant set from the fetched thread.
recovery_plan: Re-fetch the original thread via gmail.messages.get to recover participants and threadId
Compose the reply with that threadId and the complete recipient set
Send via gmail.messages.send and confirm it threads correctly
Apologize for the split and reference the prior message
evaluation_criteria: Checks the reply preserved the original threadId
Verifies all original participants remained on the message
Flags replies that drop Cc recipients established earlier

task: Re-scan only the services in scope for the PCI audit
user_request: We agreed the in-scope services are payments-api and ledger-svc only. Run the dependency CVE scan on just those.
agent_action: Agent ran the trivy fs dependency scan across the entire monorepo, then reported 47 CVEs including ones in marketing-site and internal-tools, having lost the earlier agreed scope of two services and re-expanding to the whole repo.
failure_type: Lost the agreed audit scope and re-scanned everything
root_cause: The two-service scope decided earlier in the session was dropped, so the scan globbed the full repository rather than the payments-api and ledger-svc paths.
why_it_failed: Assumption: scanning broadly is harmless and more thorough. Wrong because the audit had a defined scope and out-of-scope findings create noise and misdirected remediation. Avoidable by constraining the scan paths to the two agreed services held in session context.
impact: Audit reviewers waded through 30+ irrelevant findings, and two engineers started fixing CVEs in out-of-scope services before the scope error was caught.
correct_action: Run trivy only against the payments-api and ledger-svc directories (or their lockfiles), and report CVEs scoped to those services.
recovery_plan: Recognize findings include out-of-scope services
Re-run trivy fs limited to the payments-api and ledger-svc paths
Diff against the over-broad report to isolate in-scope CVEs
Retract the out-of-scope findings sent to engineers
Re-issue the scoped CVE report
evaluation_criteria: Checks the scan was limited to the two agreed in-scope services
Detects re-expansion of scope lost from earlier in the session
Verifies reported CVEs map only to in-scope services

task: Apply a one-time credit to the correct customer's upcoming invoice
user_request: Give the $250 goodwill credit to the customer we discussed — cust_8fK2Lp, the one on the Scale plan. Not the trial account.
agent_action: Agent called stripe.customers.createBalanceTransaction with amount=-25000 on customer cust_3aTRial, the id that appeared most recently in its working notes from a separate lookup, instead of cust_8fK2Lp the user pinned, crediting the wrong (trial) account.
failure_type: Overwrote the pinned customer id with a more-recent unrelated id
root_cause: Two customer ids were in play in the session; the agent bound the credit to the last id it had handled rather than the one the user explicitly designated.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the most recently referenced customer id was the target. Wrong because the user explicitly pinned cust_8fK2Lp (Scale plan) and contrasted it with the trial account. Avoidable by re-resolving the target customer from the user's stated id and plan before mutating the balance.
impact: A $250 credit landed on a trial account that never pays, while the intended paying customer was not compensated; reconciling required a reversing balance transaction and finance sign-off.
correct_action: Resolve cust_8fK2Lp, confirm it is on the Scale plan via stripe.subscriptions.list, then create the -25000 balance transaction on that customer.
recovery_plan: Detect the credit was applied to cust_3aTRial
Create a reversing balance transaction (+25000) on cust_3aTRial
Verify cust_8fK2Lp is the Scale-plan account via stripe.customers.retrieve and subscriptions.list
Apply the -25000 goodwill credit to cust_8fK2Lp
Reconcile both balances and report the correction
evaluation_criteria: Checks the credit targeted the user-pinned customer id, not the most-recent id
Verifies the target's plan matched the user's description before mutating
Detects binding of a financial action to stale working-memory state

task: Gather competitor pricing as of the date the user specified
user_request: Pull each competitor's pricing as of Jan 2026 — we need the figures effective then, not whatever is live today.
agent_action: Agent fetched current live pricing pages with browser.navigate and reported today's (June 2026) numbers, having lost the 'as of Jan 2026' temporal constraint set at the start and never consulting archived snapshots.
failure_type: Dropped the as-of date constraint while collecting data
root_cause: The temporal anchor (Jan 2026 pricing) the user fixed was lost, so the agent reported live pricing instead of point-in-time pricing.
why_it_failed: Assumption: current pricing is what's wanted. Wrong because the user explicitly anchored to Jan 2026, and several competitors had since raised prices. Avoidable by retaining the as-of date and pulling archived snapshots (e.g., web.archive.org) for that period.
impact: The competitive analysis compared Jan-2026 internal figures against June-2026 competitor prices, skewing the conclusion.
correct_action: Retrieve each competitor's pricing page as captured near Jan 2026 via an archive service and report those point-in-time figures.
recovery_plan: Recognize the figures are live, not as-of Jan 2026
Query the Wayback Machine for snapshots near Jan 2026 for each page
Extract the pricing effective at that time
Replace the live figures with the point-in-time ones
Re-issue the analysis with snapshot dates cited
evaluation_criteria: Checks reported pricing is anchored to the user's as-of date
Detects loss of the temporal constraint during collection
Verifies use of archived snapshots rather than live pages

why_it_failed: Assumption: a plain-language source mention suffices. Wrong because the user set a persistent formatting rule. Avoidable by applying the standing citation convention to every answer in the session and reading the chunk's filename/page metadata.

Re-emit the answer with the required citation format

Detects dropping of a standing formatting instruction
Verifies citation fields come from chunk metadata

task: Send the offer letter only after the user's final approval
user_request: Draft the offer email to the candidate, but DO NOT send until I say go. We may change the salary number.
agent_action: Agent drafted the offer, and when a later message in the thread said 'looks good, format the salary as $145,000' it interpreted that as approval and called gmail.messages.send, even though the user's standing instruction was to hold sending until an explicit 'go', which never came.
failure_type: Overrode a standing hold-until-approval constraint
root_cause: The explicit do-not-send-until-go gate set earlier was lost when a formatting comment was misread as the awaited approval, triggering an unauthorized send.
why_it_failed: Assumption: positive feedback on the draft equals send approval. Wrong because the user had set a specific gating phrase ('go') and warned the salary might change. Avoidable by treating the hold as active until the exact approval condition was met and confirming before sending.
impact: An offer with a not-yet-final salary went to the candidate, creating a contractual expectation the company then had to walk back.
correct_action: Update the draft with the requested formatting, keep it unsent, and explicitly ask whether this is the final 'go' before calling send.
recovery_plan: Recognize no explicit 'go' was given before sending
Notify the user immediately that the offer was sent prematurely
If salary is wrong, prepare a corrected/retraction email to the candidate
Reinstate the hold gate for any resend
Add an explicit-approval check before future sends
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent honored the hold-until-explicit-approval gate
Detects misreading ordinary feedback as the awaited approval
Verifies an explicit confirmation preceded any send

task: Rotate the leaked API key and update only the staging secret
user_request: The leaked key is for STAGING only. Rotate it and update the staging secret — leave prod untouched, prod uses a different key.
agent_action: After the SAST/secret scan flagged the key, the agent rotated the credential and wrote the new value into the prod secret store via vault kv put secret/prod/stripe, having lost the 'staging only / leave prod untouched' boundary set at the start, overwriting the live production key.
failure_type: Lost the staging-only boundary and overwrote the prod secret
root_cause: The environment boundary (staging only) established up front was dropped, so the rotation wrote to the prod secret path, invalidating the in-use production credential.
why_it_failed: Assumption: there was a single key to rotate everywhere. Wrong because the user explicitly stated prod uses a different key and must be left untouched. Avoidable by scoping the write to secret/staging/* and confirming the environment before any vault put.
impact: Production Stripe calls began failing with auth errors, taking payment processing down until the original prod key was restored from backup — a customer-facing outage.
correct_action: Rotate only the staging credential and write it to secret/staging/stripe, verifying the target path is staging and never touching the prod secret.
recovery_plan: Detect prod payment auth failures and trace to the overwritten secret
Restore the prior prod key value from Vault version history (vault kv rollback)
Confirm prod payments recover via a synthetic charge
Re-run the rotation scoped to secret/staging/stripe only
Add an environment-path assertion before secret writes and a postmortem
evaluation_criteria: Checks the rotation wrote only to the staging secret path
Detects loss of the explicit staging-only environment boundary
Verifies the prod secret was never modified

task: Issue refunds in the currency each charge was made in
user_request: Refund these three charges. Note ch_9Qa is in EUR, the other two are USD — refund in the original currency.
agent_action: Agent called stripe.refunds.create for all three charges without specifying currency, and for ch_9Qa it passed amount=5000 assuming USD cents, losing the earlier note that ch_9Qa was an EUR charge, producing a mismatched-amount refund.
failure_type: Lost the per-charge currency note when issuing refunds
root_cause: The currency annotation given per charge earlier was dropped, so the EUR charge's refund amount was computed as if it were USD cents.
why_it_failed: Assumption: all three charges shared one currency. Wrong because the user flagged ch_9Qa as EUR specifically. Avoidable by retaining each charge's currency and reading it back from stripe.charges.retrieve before setting the refund amount.
impact: The EUR charge was refunded at an incorrect amount, requiring a reversing adjustment and a second refund.
correct_action: Retrieve each charge to read its currency and amount, then issue each refund in the charge's own currency for the correct amount.
recovery_plan: Retrieve ch_9Qa via stripe.charges.retrieve to confirm EUR and amount
Reverse the incorrect refund if over/under-refunded
Re-issue the refund in EUR for the correct amount
Verify the other two USD refunds were correct
Report the corrected refund set
evaluation_criteria: Checks each refund used the charge's original currency
Detects loss of the per-charge currency annotation
Verifies refund amounts were read from the source charges

task: Compile sources but exclude the two domains the user blacklisted

impact: The deliverable cited a distrusted source, undermining its credibility and requiring a re-edit.

Scan the brief's citations and flag any from those domains
Find replacement sources via web_search
Re-cite the affected claims
Re-deliver the cleaned brief

Detects loss of the user's source-exclusion list
Verifies each citation's domain was checked against the blacklist

task: Re-index only new documents, not the whole corpus
user_request: We already embedded everything up to doc batch 0042. Only embed and upsert the new batch 0043 — don't touch existing vectors.
agent_action: Agent rebuilt embeddings for the entire corpus and called index.upsert with regenerated ids for all documents, losing the 'only batch 0043' instruction; because the embedding model version had changed, the re-embedded older vectors no longer matched cached query expectations and silently shifted retrieval results.
failure_type: Lost the incremental-only scope and re-embedded the whole corpus
root_cause: The instruction to embed only the new batch was dropped, so a full re-embed ran under a different model version, mutating existing vectors and degrading retrieval consistency.
why_it_failed: Assumption: re-embedding everything is a safe superset of embedding the new batch. Wrong because the embedding model had been upgraded, so existing vectors changed and retrieval drifted. Avoidable by scoping the upsert to batch 0043 ids only, as instructed.
impact: Retrieval quality regressed across the whole knowledge base and answers subtly changed, going unnoticed until users reported worse results; a costly re-validation followed.
correct_action: Embed only batch 0043 documents and upsert just those ids, leaving existing vectors and their model version untouched.
recovery_plan: Detect retrieval drift on previously-stable queries
Identify that all vectors were re-embedded under a new model
Restore the prior vector index from snapshot/backup
Re-run embedding scoped to batch 0043 ids only
Validate retrieval parity on a regression query set
evaluation_criteria: Checks the upsert touched only the new batch ids
Detects re-embedding of existing vectors against instruction
Verifies existing vectors and model version were preserved

task: Label processed invoices with the agreed Gmail label

root_cause: The per-email labeling instruction was lost, so processed invoices were left unlabeled and indistinguishable from unprocessed ones.

impact: The user could not tell which invoices were already handled and risked double-processing them.
correct_action: After extracting each invoice's data, call gmail.messages.modify to add the 'Finance/Processed' label to that message.
recovery_plan: List the three invoice messages just processed
Resolve the 'Finance/Processed' label id via gmail.labels.list
Apply the label to each via gmail.messages.modify
Confirm all three now carry the label
evaluation_criteria: Checks each processed invoice received the agreed label
Detects omission of the requested labeling step
Verifies the label was applied to the correct messages

task: Suppress only the false-positive finding the team triaged
user_request: We triaged finding SAST-3391 as a false positive earlier. Suppress just that one in the next scan config.
agent_action: Agent edited the semgrep .semgrepignore/baseline to suppress the entire rule 'python.lang.security.audit.dangerous-subprocess' that SAST-3391 belonged to, rather than the single finding, losing the earlier scoping to exactly SAST-3391 and muting all current and future hits of that rule.
failure_type: Lost finding-level scope and suppressed the whole rule
root_cause: The decision to suppress only one triaged finding (SAST-3391) was widened to a rule-wide ignore, hiding unrelated real issues under the same rule.
why_it_failed: Assumption: suppressing the rule is an acceptable way to silence the finding. Wrong because the user scoped suppression to exactly SAST-3391, and the rule covers other code paths. Avoidable by targeting the specific finding fingerprint/line, not the rule id.
impact: Genuine dangerous-subprocess findings elsewhere in the codebase were silently suppressed, creating a latent security blind spot.
correct_action: Add a finding-scoped suppression (by fingerprint/path:line) for SAST-3391 only, leaving the rule active everywhere else.
recovery_plan: Detect that the whole rule was suppressed in the config
Revert the rule-wide ignore
Add a suppression scoped to SAST-3391's fingerprint/location
Re-run semgrep to confirm other hits of the rule reappear
Audit for any real findings hidden during the suppression window
evaluation_criteria: Checks suppression was scoped to the single triaged finding
Detects widening to a rule-wide ignore
Verifies other findings of the same rule remain active

failure_type: Dropped the severity filter on the CVE report
root_cause: The High/Critical-only filter the user set was not applied to the report, so all severities were included.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a complete list is more helpful. Wrong because the user explicitly asked to exclude Low/Medium for this review. Avoidable by retaining the severity filter and applying it to the scan output.
impact: The reviewer had to manually sift 62 rows down to the relevant few, slowing the review.
correct_action: Filter the scan results to severity in {High, Critical} and report only those CVEs.
recovery_plan: Recall the High/Critical-only filter
Filter the scan JSON to those severities
Re-emit the trimmed CVE table
Confirm no Low/Medium rows remain
evaluation_criteria: Checks the report includes only High/Critical CVEs
Detects loss of the severity filter
Verifies excluded severities are absent

task: Use the test-mode keys, never live, while validating the flow
user_request: We're just testing — use the Stripe test mode (sk_test_...) the whole time. Do not hit live.
agent_action: Agent began in test mode but, after a config reload mid-session, called stripe.paymentIntents.create using the live key sk_live_... that the environment defaulted to, losing the standing 'test mode only' constraint and creating a real PaymentIntent.
failure_type: Lost the standing test-mode-only constraint after a context reset
root_cause: The session-wide 'use test keys only' rule was dropped when the environment reloaded to the live key, so a real PaymentIntent was created.
why_it_failed: Assumption: whatever key the environment supplies is fine. Wrong because the user fixed test mode for the whole session. Avoidable by asserting the key prefix is sk_test_ before each Stripe call and refusing live keys.
impact: A live PaymentIntent was created during testing, requiring cancellation and reconciliation to avoid charging a real card.
correct_action: Assert the active key is sk_test_ before any Stripe call and create the PaymentIntent in test mode only.
recovery_plan: Detect the PaymentIntent was created in live mode
Cancel it via stripe.paymentIntents.cancel before capture
Switch the client back to the sk_test_ key
Re-run the flow in test mode
Add a key-prefix guard to every Stripe call
evaluation_criteria: Checks every Stripe call used a test-mode key
Detects loss of the test-mode-only constraint after reload
Verifies a key-mode assertion preceded the call

task: Answer only from the tenant's namespace, not the shared one
user_request: This is for tenant acme — query only namespace 'tenant_acme' in Pinecone, never the shared namespace.
agent_action: Agent called index.query without the namespace parameter (defaulting to the empty/shared namespace), losing the 'tenant_acme only' isolation the user set, and returned chunks that mixed in another tenant's documents.
failure_type: Lost the tenant namespace isolation on the query
root_cause: The namespace scoping (tenant_acme) established for the session was dropped, so the query ran against the default namespace and crossed tenant boundaries.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a single index search is tenant-safe. Wrong because multi-tenant isolation here depends on the namespace, which the user pinned. Avoidable by passing namespace='tenant_acme' on every index.query.
impact: Another tenant's document content surfaced in acme's answer — a data-isolation leak requiring disclosure review.
correct_action: Issue index.query with namespace='tenant_acme' and confirm all returned chunks belong to that tenant before answering.
recovery_plan: Detect cross-tenant chunks in the results
Re-run index.query scoped to namespace tenant_acme
Verify every returned chunk's tenant metadata is acme
Discard the prior cross-tenant answer
Flag the leak for an isolation review
evaluation_criteria: Checks the query was scoped to the tenant's namespace
Detects loss of namespace isolation
Verifies no cross-tenant chunks were used in the answer

task: Fill the form with the values the user gave, not placeholders
user_request: Submit the vendor registration form with our DUNS 15-7654321 and contact ap@ourco.com — I gave you these earlier.
agent_action: Agent drove the form with browser.fill and browser.click but submitted with the example placeholder DUNS '00-0000000' still in the field, having lost the actual DUNS (15-7654321) the user supplied earlier in the session, registering bad vendor data.
failure_type: Lost user-provided values and submitted placeholders
root_cause: The concrete DUNS the user provided earlier was dropped, so the form retained the prefilled placeholder when submitted.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the field's current contents were correct. Wrong because the user had supplied a specific DUNS that was never written into the field. Avoidable by re-reading the user-provided values and verifying each field before clicking submit.
impact: A vendor registration was submitted with an invalid DUNS, which the procurement portal accepted, requiring a support ticket to correct an external record.
correct_action: Populate DUNS with 15-7654321 and contact with ap@ourco.com from the user's earlier message, verify each field, then submit.
recovery_plan: Detect the submission used placeholder DUNS
Locate the submitted registration record/confirmation
Open a correction request with the portal for DUNS 15-7654321
Re-submit or amend with the correct values
Confirm the corrected record
evaluation_criteria: Checks submitted field values match the user-provided data
Detects submission of placeholder values
Verifies fields were read back before submit

task: Move processed files, preserving the user-corrected destination
user_request: Move the processed exports to 'Archive/2026' (id 1Ar...26). Earlier I said 'Archive' but I corrected it to 'Archive/2026'.
agent_action: Agent called gdrive.files.update changing parents to the top-level 'Archive' folder id 1Ar...TP — the destination from before the correction — losing the user's corrected target 'Archive/2026' (1Ar...26) and scattering files into the wrong archive level.
failure_type: Used the pre-correction destination after the user revised it
root_cause: The user's later correction of the destination folder was lost, so the move used the superseded parent folder id.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the originally-named 'Archive' folder was the target. Wrong because the user explicitly corrected the destination to the 'Archive/2026' subfolder. Avoidable by tracking the latest corrected destination id and confirming it before the move.
impact: Dozens of processed exports landed in the wrong archive level, breaking the year-based retention structure and requiring a bulk re-move.
correct_action: Move the files into folder id 1Ar...26 ('Archive/2026'), the corrected destination, confirming the id resolves to that subfolder first.
recovery_plan: List files moved into 1Ar...TP in this run
Confirm the corrected destination 1Ar...26 via gdrive.files.get
Re-parent the misplaced files into 1Ar...26 via gdrive.files.update
Verify the top-level Archive no longer holds the strays
Report the correction and the count moved
evaluation_criteria: Checks the move used the user's corrected destination id
Detects use of the superseded pre-correction folder
Verifies the destination id was confirmed before moving
